explanations: luna: This ayah states that God intends ease rather than hardship in the Ramadan fast. Its own setting is fasting, the same passage as 2:187's permitted nighttime intimacy, and it reuses the section's ease/difficulty pairing in a context independent of a child's sex. | terra: God desires ease, not hardship, in the fasting passage whose night, marital approach, and dawn are developed two ayat later in 2:187.

luna: The section itself cites this ayah: spouses are reciprocally called لباس, and intimacy is permitted through the fasting night until dawn separates white from black. It joins the section's marital covering to the night/day boundary. | terra: Fasting nights permit marital approach, call each spouse the other's garment, and end when the white dawn-thread separates from the black, joining sexual covering to daylight's disclosure.

luna: The section's B004 dictionary wording أتيته (“I came to that place”) is offered as a euphemism for intercourse; this ayah uses فَأْتُوا in its marital intercourse instruction and places it beside fertility imagery. It makes the section's “coming” euphemism concrete in a reproductive setting. | terra: Calling wives a tilth links marital approach to the possibility of generation, a different bodily figure for the section's movement from covering to pregnancy.
terra: Divorced women may not conceal what God has created in their wombs, joining hidden pregnancy, divine creation, and the marital boundary within one legal scene.
terra: It is generally unlawful to take back anything given to wives at divorce, reinforcing the bridal gift as a protected transfer rather than a temporary price.
terra: Nursing, the father's provision and clothing, and the ban on harming either parent through the child extend birth into reciprocal duties of giving.
terra: Divorce before touching or fixing a bridal due still requires a fair gift according to means, separating marital giving from consummation.
terra: When a due was fixed but the marriage ends before touching, half remains owed unless freely waived, defining the bridal gift at the boundary of sexual union.
terra: Divorced women are owed a fair provision as a duty upon the God-conscious, extending giving beyond union and tying it to taqwā.
terra: God forms people in wombs however He wills, joining hidden formation and divine choice behind the male-female child.

luna: The section recalls the wife of Imran dedicating what is in her womb (مَا فِي بَطْنِي) to God; this ayah is that vow. It sets the expected child's birth inside an act of offering. | terra: Imran's wife vows the unborn child in her womb to God, providing the faithful prenatal promise against which the couple's broken promise in 7:189-190 can be read.

luna: The section quotes the mother saying وَضَعْتُهَا أُنثَىٰ and the Quran's reply that God knows what she bore. This ayah's own words name the newborn girl and place the birth within divine knowledge. | terra: The mother delivers a female and voices a male-female distinction, but God's intervening knowledge and Mary's naming prevent her femaleness from fixing her worth.

luna: This ayah says her Lord accepted Mary with good acceptance (بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ), completing 3:36's birth of a girl. That acceptance reverses the social devaluation the section sets beside female birth. | terra: God accepts the girl with a beautiful acceptance, gives her beautiful growth, and provides for her, completing 3:36's reversal of disappointment at a female birth.
terra: Zechariah asks God for good offspring as a gift from Him, closely echoing the couple's request for a ṣāliḥ child in 7:189.
terra: The answer grants John as a son who confirms a word from God, bringing a bestowed child and the ṣ-d-q act of confirmation into the same birth announcement.
terra: Mary receives glad tidings of a divinely given child, placing the son's identity inside God's gift and decree before conception rather than inside a human preference for males.
terra: Mary asks how she can have a child when no man has touched her, and the answer says God creates what He wills; this marks an explicit exception to the section's union-to-birth sequence.

luna: This ayah says God does not waste the work of any worker, male or female, and that they are from one another. Its context rewards faithfulness under persecution; the link is the section's shift from sex as a birth measure to conduct and devotion as the measure. | terra: God wastes no deed of any worker, male or female, because each is of the other, explicitly denying that sex determines the outcome of striving.

luna: This ayah describes humanity created from one soul and its mate, then spread as many men and women. It is a broader creation-and-couple parallel to the first couple in 7:189 and the paired sexes in the section. | terra: One soul and its mate become many men and women, while the ayah invokes the wombs, connecting the pair's creation to kinship generated through birth.

luna: The section explicitly distinguishes the root ص د ق's mahr branch from 92:6's “affirm”; this ayah commands, وَآتُوا النِّسَاءَ صَدُقَاتِهِنَّ. It is the direct Quranic wording for the bride's dower as something given to her. | terra: The command to give women their ṣaduqāt as a free gift places the source section's secondary ṣ-d-q sense, bridal due, and the surah's act of giving in one concrete marriage scene.
terra: Men may neither inherit women against their will nor constrain wives to recover part of what was given them, so marriage-giving cannot become a means of possessing or devaluing the woman.
terra: Even a very large bridal gift may not be reclaimed when one wife is replaced by another, protecting the giving that attends marriage.
terra: The prohibition on taking the gift back is grounded in spouses having gone intimately to one another and in the wife's solemn covenant.
terra: Lawful marriage requires seeking women in chastity and giving them their due compensation, another direct Qur'anic formulation of the bridal gift.
terra: Marriage to believing bondwomen requires family permission and fair payment of their bridal dues, extending the section's gift obligation across social rank.

luna: This ayah promises entry to the Garden to believing men or women who do right, with no injustice to them. It is a further direct statement that moral standing does not follow the male/female distinction at the center of the section. | terra: A believer who acts rightly, male or female, enters the Garden without injustice, repeating the section's replacement of sex with action as the decisive measure.
terra: Marriage to chaste believing or scriptural women is lawful when their bridal dues are given, again binding union to an actual gift.

luna: The section gives the root ه د ي a bridal dictionary sense, “the bride was led to her husband”; this ayah uses يَهْدِيهِمْ for God's guidance along paths of peace and out of darkness into light. The bridge is modest because the ayah describes spiritual guidance, while the section activates the root's concrete sense of leading someone to a destination.
terra: When night غَشِيَ Abraham, it literally covers a person; this supplies the ordinary covering sense from which the section hears the verb's sexual usage.
terra: God cleaves the dawn, makes night for rest, and measures sun and moon, joining the section's dawn disclosure and dark repose to divine determination.

terra: The production of humanity from one soul followed by a place of settlement and a repository may echo generation and hidden keeping, although the two locations admit interpretations broader than the womb.
terra: People fabricate sons and daughters for God without knowledge, while He is exalted above their associations; the Creator of the sexes is not assigned offspring by them.
terra: The Creator of everything is asked how He could have a child without a consort, marking divine creation as categorically beyond the pair-to-birth sequence in creatures.
terra: The pagan rule assigning what is in cattle wombs to males but barring wives, with another rule for stillbirth, exposes arbitrary male-female valuation attached to the womb.

terra: Those who kill their children foolishly and forbid God's provision are declared lost, connecting rejection of a child with the same refusal of divine gift and provision that the section opposes.
terra: The question whether God forbade the two males, the two females, or what the females' wombs contain dismantles invented sex-based rules by demanding knowledge.
terra: The same male-female-womb interrogation is repeated for camels and cattle, completing the challenge to manufactured gender distinctions.
terra: The command not to kill children from poverty is grounded in God's provision for parents and children, opposing economic withholding to the reception of birth as gift.
terra: Night rapidly covers day with يُغْشِى, restaging the cosmic cover that the section maps onto marital approach.
terra: Moses asks to look and God تَجَلَّىٰ to the mountain; manifestation and attempted sight give the section's bridal 'unveiling so the husband looks' a weighty contrasting use of the same root.

luna: The section's B004 dictionary form غشيان names intercourse as covering; this ayah uses تَغَشَّاهَا for the first couple's union, then says she conceived a light burden. It carries the section's covering image directly into pregnancy. | terra: The single soul's mate, sexual covering in تَغَشَّاهَا, pregnancy, and the couple's request for a sound child enact the section's full movement from covering to conception and promised gratitude.

luna: The next ayah says the child was given, then the parents associated partners with what He gave; فَتَعَالَى اللَّهُ also uses the root ع ل و named for 92:20's الْأَعْلَى. It completes the section's union-to-birth-to-gift sequence with a failure of gratitude. | terra: After the child is given, the couple associates partners in the gift; paired with 7:189, this is the section's broken parental promise, while فَتَعَالَى reaches the same height-root as al-Aʿlā.
terra: Believing men and women are allies who together establish prayer and give alms, putting both sexes on the giving side of the surah's moral divide.
terra: The same believing men and women are promised the same gardens and divine pleasure, completing 9:71's shared action with a shared end.
terra: Faces of wrongdoers seem covered with pieces of dark night, giving literal Qur'anic form to the section's reading of night descending upon the face darkened at a daughter's news.
terra: Night is made for rest and day made visible, a functional night-day pair that supports the section's covering and disclosure pattern.
terra: Abraham's standing wife receives glad tidings of Isaac and then Jacob, staging motherhood and lineage as an unexpected divine announcement.
terra: She asks how she can bear while old and her husband aged, marking the biological limit that the promised birth crosses.
terra: The messengers answer by invoking God's mercy and blessing on the household, interpreting the unlikely child as bestowed grace.

luna: The section names the root غ ش و for covering and joins night/day to a male/female pair; this ayah says يُغْشِي اللَّيْلَ النَّهَارَ and also speaks of fruits made in pairs. It brings covering and paired creation into one scene. | terra: Every fruit is made a pair and night covers day in the same ayah, a close Qur'anic meeting of the section's paired creation and غ ش و covering.

luna: This ayah says God knows what every female carries (مَا تَحْمِلُ كُلُّ أُنثَىٰ) and what wombs decrease or increase. It expands the section's birth scene and its 3:36 line that God knows what the mother delivered. | terra: God knows what every female bears, every contraction and increase of the womb, and holds everything by measure, directly developing the section's hidden and measured formation.
terra: Abraham praises God for granting Ishmael and Isaac despite old age, explicitly receiving sons as gifts rather than achievements or status tokens.
terra: Abraham's visitors announce a knowledgeable boy, another direct formulation of a son received as divine glad tidings.
terra: Abraham responds that old age has reached him and asks how such news can hold, stating the reproductive improbability within the announcement.
terra: The messengers affirm the glad tidings as true and tell him not to despair, making hope in divine giving the answer to bodily improbability.
terra: Human creation from a drop supplies another terse formulation of the bodily origin underlying the male-female pair.
terra: The direction of the path is said to belong to God while some ways deviate, closely paralleling the divine stance of 'upon Us is guidance' that the section also hears as leading to arrival.

luna: This ayah says the people assign daughters to God while keeping what they desire for themselves. It sets the gendered preference that 16:58 shows on a father's face, the same value scale the section overturns. | terra: People assign daughters to God while reserving what they desire for themselves, setting up the dark-faced daughter announcement in 16:58.

luna: This ayah says a man darkens when told of a female child (بِالْأُنثَىٰ ... مُسْوَدًّا). The section explicitly likens that darkness on the face to night and names the same female-birth word, exposing the valuation it later dissolves. | terra: The face of the man given news of a female child turns black as he suppresses grief, staging exactly the gendered value scale that the section says the surah dislodges.

luna: This ayah completes 16:58: the father weighs keeping the girl in disgrace against burying her in the ground. That is the concrete harm behind the section's rejected ranking of male and female birth. | terra: The man hides from people and deliberates whether to keep the girl in humiliation or bury her, carrying 16:58's darkened face into the social violence of the preference.

luna: This ayah connects spouses made from among people with sons and grandchildren and with provision. It supplies a household sequence—pairing, offspring, provision—that complements the section's bride, birth, and gift images. | terra: God makes spouses from people's own kind and gives children, grandchildren, and provision, joining pair, offspring, and gift.
terra: God brings people from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing and gives hearing, sight, and hearts so they may be grateful, joining birth as gift with the gratitude promised in 7:189.

luna: This ayah promises a good life and reward for whoever acts rightly, male or female, while believing. It makes the section's displacement of gendered worth by faithful action explicit in another context. | terra: Any believer who acts rightly, male or female, receives a good life and reward, making conduct rather than sex the path to good outcome.
terra: The night and day are two signs: the night-sign is effaced and the day-sign made visible so people may seek bounty and reckon time, elaborating cover, disclosure, provision, and measure.
terra: The ban on killing children for fear of poverty is grounded in God's provision for child and parent, opposing refusal of the child-gift through anxiety about giving.

luna: This ayah rebukes the claim that God chose sons for the people while taking female angels for Himself. Its own subject is angelic attribution rather than human birth, but the self-serving male/female valuation directly echoes the section's rejected preference for sons. | terra: The question whether God favored people with sons while taking female angels for Himself exposes the contradiction in their preferred-sex theology.
terra: One man reminds another that God created him from dust, then a drop, then fashioned him as a man, another compact route from generative matter to embodied human form.
terra: Zechariah names his wife's barrenness while asking God for an heir, making the hoped-for child a gift across a concrete reproductive limit.
terra: The announcement of John answers Zechariah's request with a named boy bestowed through divine glad tidings.
terra: Zechariah asks how a boy is possible with a barren wife and his own extreme age, stating the bodily obstacle that the gift crosses.
terra: God calls this birth easy for Him and recalls Zechariah's prior creation from nothing, locating yusr in divine creative power rather than in the child's male sex.
terra: The messenger announces that a pure boy will be bestowed on Mary, making a child explicitly a divine gift while opening a birth outside ordinary coupling.
terra: Mary's question that no man has touched her marks a boundary to the section's ordinary movement from male-female union to conception.
terra: The virgin birth is easy for God, a decreed sign and mercy, relocating ease in divine power rather than in the sex of the child.
terra: Mary conceives and withdraws to a distant place, moving the exceptional conception of 19:20-21 into an actual pregnancy.

luna: This ayah places Mary in labor pains at a palm trunk. It is a distinct Quranic childbirth scene that gives bodily force to the section's dictionary detail for difficult birth; this verse itself centers the labor. | terra: Labor drives Mary to the palm trunk and makes her wish she had been forgotten; a son's birth is thus the Qur'an's clearest reversal of the proverb that links boys with easy labor.

luna: The next ayah tells Mary not to grieve and mentions a stream below her. Its own contribution is relief and provision immediately after the labor scene in 19:23. | terra: At the point of severe labor, Mary is consoled and given water, beginning the provision that meets rather than denies birth's hardship.

luna: This ayah tells Mary to shake the palm trunk so ripe dates fall to her. It continues 19:23's childbirth scene with food provided to the mother after labor, joining burden to gift. | terra: Fresh dates are made available to Mary during labor, adding bodily provision to the consolation of 19:24.

luna: This ayah tells Mary to eat, drink, and be comforted after the birth scene. It completes the immediate care sequence following labor, a specific continuation of the section's birth image. | terra: After Mary's labor she is told to eat, drink, and be comforted, completing the preceding water-and-dates scene as provision for the mother after difficult birth.
terra: In the immediate Mary-and-Jesus context, God does not take a son; He creates by decree, bounding the section's ordinary reproductive imagery at divine agency.
terra: Moses says the Lord gave each thing its creation and then guided it, making guidance the carrying-forward of a creature's given form and fitness.
terra: Zechariah's prayer not to be left childless frames offspring as a hoped-for divine provision rather than a human entitlement.
terra: God answers, gives John, and repairs his wife for him, explicitly presenting fertility and the child as gifts met by reverent hope and fear.
terra: Mary guards her chastity, God breathes into her, and mother and son become a sign, preserving the virgin birth as an explicit exception to ordinary coupling.
terra: The Last Hour makes every pregnant woman lay down her load, a catastrophic interruption of pregnancy that marks a boundary to ordinary delivery.

luna: The section's B003 dictionary gloss takes مُخَلَّقَةٌ as fully formed flesh in the womb; 22:5 uses مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ for a womb-lump. It anchors the shared root while preserving the ayah's contrast between formed and unformed. | terra: The sequence from drop to clot to مُضْغَةٍ مُّخَلَّقَةٍ, retention in wombs, and birth names the formed flesh-piece behind the section's dictionary sense of creation.
terra: Creation of the human from an extract of clay supplies the first stage of the sequence continued by the womb lodging in 23:13 and embryonic formation in 23:14.
terra: The drop is placed in a firm lodging, giving the womb-stage that 23:14 then unfolds into successive acts of creation.

luna: This ayah names a مُّضْغَةً and describes its development into bones clothed with flesh. It is a direct Quranic womb scene for the section's dictionary discussion of mudghah and formation. | terra: The clot, flesh-piece, bones, flesh, and another creation expand the section's formed mudgha into a sequence of divine shaping.
terra: Female and male sexual offenders receive the same stated punishment, a legal boundary around sexual approach in which sex does not alter accountability.
terra: Corrupt and good women and men are paired by moral description, shifting the decisive correspondence between the sexes from sex itself to character.

luna: This ayah restricts displaying women's adornment and names husbands among those to whom it may be shown. It parallels the section's dictionary image of a bride adorned and shown to her husband, while adding a boundary around who may see. | terra: Women's adornment is to remain covered from the public but may be shown to husbands, giving a legal boundary for the section's scene of bridal disclosure and spousal looking.
terra: Three household privacy times—before dawn prayer, midday undressing, and after night prayer—bring clothing, intimacy, night, and daylight thresholds into one domestic scene.

luna: This ayah calls night a garment (لِبَاسًا) and day a rising/spreading forth. The section's spouses-as-garments image and night/day opening meet in a direct parallel. | terra: Night is made a garment and day a rising, reinforcing the section's meeting of marital garment, nocturnal covering, and daylight emergence.
terra: The prayer for spouses and offspring as a comfort to the eyes presents family as a requested gift and sight as delight rather than the darkened face of unwanted birth.

terra: The queen's هَدِيَّة is a gift dispatched to a recipient; this may faintly illuminate the h-d-y family's sense of something borne toward another, alongside the bride being led and gifted in the source section.

terra: Solomon refuses the dispatched gift because God's giving is better; with 27:35 this may clarify the difference between human هدِيَّة and divine bestowal, though the bridal link remains indirect.
terra: The Midianite father offers one daughter to Moses in a marriage agreement whose required service functions as the concrete bridal consideration.
terra: Moses accepts the marriage terms as an agreement between the two men, completing 28:27's scene of a bride being joined to her husband.
terra: Night for rest and day for seeking divine bounty are paired so people may give thanks, linking the section's cover-and-disclosure cycle with provision and gratitude.

luna: This ayah says God made spouses from among people so they may find tranquility in one another, with affection and mercy between them. It adds the relational purpose of the bride-and-husband union developed in the section. | terra: Spouses created from yourselves provide tranquility, affection, and mercy, stating what the section's male-female approach and bridal joining are for.

luna: This ayah describes a mother carrying her child in weakness upon weakness and weaning him in two years. It gives the section's birth-and-hardship image a second, sustained account of maternal burden. | terra: The mother's weakness upon weakness in carrying and weaning grounds gratitude in the cost of maternity without assigning that cost by the child's sex.
terra: Knowledge of what is in the wombs belongs to God, reinforcing the section's hidden pregnancy as a domain of divine knowledge.
terra: Human progeny is made from an extract of lowly fluid, another direct account of generation from the sexual drop.
terra: God proportions the human and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, extending reproductive origin into fitted life and the demand for gratitude.
terra: Men and women are paired across submission, truthfulness, patience, charity, fasting, chastity, and remembrance, then given the same forgiveness and reward.
terra: God says He married Zaynab to the Prophet after Zayd's bond ended, giving a direct Qur'anic instance of a woman being joined to a husband.
terra: A marriage dissolved before touching has no waiting period, yet the woman must be given a provision and released graciously, marking union's legal boundary while preserving giving.
terra: The Prophet's wives whose bridal dues he has given are named as lawful, tying marital union to completed giving.

luna: This ayah requires visitors to the Prophet's wives to speak from behind a screen. The link is specifically visibility in a marital setting: it sets a privacy boundary alongside the section's dictionary image of a bride displayed to her husband; the two customs are not identical. | terra: In the setting of the Prophet's marriage meal, guests must leave and address his wives from behind a screen, a wedding-context boundary to the section's image of a bride being unveiled to her husband.

luna: This ayah joins creation from a drop to being made pairs, then says no female conceives or gives birth outside God's knowledge. It makes the section's male/female pair, conception, birth, and divine giving one connected account. | terra: Creation from dust and a drop, making pairs, and the rule that no female conceives or delivers outside God's knowledge unite the section's creation, sex, and womb scenes.

luna: This ayah praises the Creator of pairs in what the earth grows, in human selves, and in what people do not know. It broadens the section's specific night/day and male/female pairs into a Quranic theme of paired creation. | terra: God creates all pairs—from the earth's growth, from human selves, and from what people do not know—placing the male-female image in a wider created pattern.
terra: Night becomes a sign when day is stripped from it and people are left in darkness, a vivid reversal of the section's daylight unveiling.
terra: A human created from a drop becomes an open disputant, another sharp juxtaposition of humble reproductive origin and later agency.
terra: Abraham asks his Lord for a child among the righteous, closely repeating the ṣāliḥ-child request carried by the section from 7:189.
terra: God gives him good news of a forbearing boy, answering the prayer and staging a son as divine glad tidings rather than as human status.

luna: This ayah asks whether daughters are assigned to God and sons to the people. It repeats the gendered allocation challenged in 16:57 and directly parallels the section's account of preferring male birth. | terra: The question 'daughters for your Lord and sons for them?' directly confronts the same preference for male offspring over female.

luna: This ayah asks whether the people witnessed the creation of angels as female, completing 37:149's challenge to their male/female allocation. It adds the question of who could know or witness that sex assignment. | terra: The question whether the angels were created female while the claimants watched joins female creation-language to a rebuke of groundless gender attribution.
terra: This ayah identifies the surrounding offspring-claim as the speakers' fabrication, clarifying that the daughter-son questions expose their lie rather than rank either sex.
terra: The explicit claim that God begot is declared false, supplying the theological boundary behind 37:149-153 between created sexual generation and the Creator.

luna: This ayah asks whether God selected daughters over sons, crystallizing the allocation questioned in 37:149 and the intervening passage. It directly exposes the same gender hierarchy that the section says God's giving dissolves. | terra: The question whether God chose daughters over sons lays bare the hierarchy presumed by the speakers rather than accepting it.
terra: 'How do you judge?' turns the preceding son-daughter allocation into an indictment of the human value judgment itself.

luna: This ayah describes God wrapping night over day and day over night. The reciprocal concealment sharpens the section's paired opposites, where night covers and day appears. | terra: God wraps night over day and day over night, a nonlexical version of the reciprocal covering and disclosure that frames the section.

luna: This ayah describes creation after creation inside mothers' wombs, within three layers of darkness. It joins the section's hidden, covering night image to gestation and formation. | terra: One soul, its mate, and creation stage after stage in three darknesses combine pairing, formation, womb, and covering in a single ayah.
terra: A believer who does right, male or female, enters the Garden and is provided without measure, joining equal moral standing with divine provision.
terra: God makes night for rest and day giving sight, another direct night-day pair structured as cover and visibility.
terra: Dust, drop, clot, emergence as a child, maturity, and old age place birth inside a divinely completed life-course.
terra: No female conceives or gives birth except with God's knowledge; the hidden reproductive event is thus held within divine knowing rather than human valuation.
terra: The Creator makes spouses from human selves and pairs among cattle by which creation multiplies, extending sexual pairing into providential increase.

luna: This ayah says God gives daughters and sons to whom He wills (يَهَبُ ... إِنَاثًا ... الذُّكُورَ). It treats both sexes as gifts, undoing the birth formula that assigned ease to boys and hardship to girls. | terra: God's gift is stated with daughters first and sons second, making either sex a divine bestowal rather than a scale of ease, honor, or misfortune.

luna: This ayah completes 42:49 by adding mixed pairs of sons and daughters and those made barren. Its own contribution is to place sex and childlessness within what God gives or withholds, as the section does. | terra: The continuation gives some both males and females and makes others barren, completing 42:49's claim that sex and fertility are apportioned by divine knowledge and power.
terra: God creates pairs of all things and provides ships and cattle to ride, extending paired creation into the gifts that carry creatures to destinations.

luna: This ayah asks whether God took daughters from what He creates while choosing sons for the people. It repeats the gendered assignment exposed in 16:57 and makes the section's male/female valuation a boundary of its own. | terra: The question whether God took daughters from what He creates while selecting sons for people exposes their gender hierarchy within the language of creation.

luna: This ayah repeats the face darkening and swallowed grief when one is given news of what he assigns to the Most Merciful; 43:16 identifies that as daughters. The repeated scene reinforces the section's image of gender bias darkening a face. | terra: A man receiving the very female child he attributes to God turns dark-faced and choked with grief, repeating and sharpening 16:58's scene.
terra: The next rhetorical description voices the culture's disparaging picture of the female child, allowing the surrounding rebuke to expose how that ranking is constructed.
terra: Calling the angels female is condemned as unwitnessed testimony, separating created sexual categories from invented claims about the unseen.

luna: This ayah says a mother carries and gives birth with hardship (كُرْهًا) and makes that labor part of the call to gratitude toward parents. It supplies the bodily cost behind the section's difficult-birth dictionary sense. | terra: A mother carries and delivers her child in hardship, making real labor-pain grounds for gratitude to her while refusing to attach that hardship specifically to a daughter.
terra: God guides and sets right those killed in His way, beginning a sequence in which guidance leads to an actual destination.
terra: God admits the guided into the Garden He has made known to them, concretely realizing hidaya as being brought to arrival.
terra: Believing men and believing women share admission to gardens and forgiveness, another outcome determined by faith rather than sex.
terra: Hypocritical and associating men and women likewise share judgment for their corrupt stance, completing 48:5's demonstration that the moral divide crosses both sexes.

luna: The ayah names creation from male and female (ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ), then locates honor with God in taqwa. It directly meets the section's reversal of a value scale that ranked a boy's birth above a girl's. | terra: Creation from a male and a female culminates in the declaration that honor is measured by taqwā, directly replacing inherited sex-ranking with the section's moral criterion.
terra: Abraham is given glad tidings of a knowledgeable boy, opening the scene whose focus then shifts to his barren wife's response.
terra: Abraham's wife strikes her face and calls herself an old barren woman, a birth-announcement face-scene whose cause is impossible fertility rather than contempt for a daughter.
terra: The messengers answer that the wise and knowing Lord has decreed the son, locating the apparently impossible birth within divine measure.
terra: Creation of all things in pairs universalizes the relational pattern that 92:3 names as male and female.
terra: 'Daughters for Him and sons for you?' is another concise exposure of assigning the devalued sex to God while reserving the valued sex for oneself.

luna: This ayah asks whether the male is for the people and the female for God (الذَّكَرُ ... الْأُنثَىٰ). Its own context concerns the assignment of divine beings, not human children, but the same unequal male/female valuation is directly challenged. | terra: The question whether males are for the hearers while females are assigned to God exposes their preferred share as a value judgment about the sexes.

luna: This ayah calls that allocation an unjust division (قِسْمَةٌ ضِيزَىٰ), completing 53:21. It gives a Quranic judgment on the same asymmetry the section exposes in the preference for sons. | terra: Calling that allocation an unjust division explicitly condemns the male-favoring scale that the section hears in the old birth formula.

luna: The section's named roots ذ ك ر and ء ن ث occur in the same male/female pair here: خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنثَىٰ. It directly joins paired creation to the section's third ayah. | terra: خَلَقَ ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ restates almost exactly the oath-image of the Creator making the male-female pair.

luna: The next ayah names a drop when it is emitted (نُطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ), moving from 53:45's male/female pair to conception, as the section does. | terra: Immediately after the male-female pair in 53:45, this ayah locates it in an emitted drop, making the section's transition from pairing to generation explicit.
terra: God's question, 'We created you,' makes the Creator rather than the parents the speaker over the reproductive scene developed in the next two ayat.
terra: The emitted seed is placed before the addressee as an observable act, matching the section's movement from union toward birth.
terra: The question whether humans create the seed or God is the Creator locates agency behind conception exactly where the oath to the Creator of male and female does.
terra: Believing men and women share light running before them toward one promised end, combining gender parity with illumination after the section's night-day frame.
terra: Hypocritical men and women together ask the believers to wait so they can take from their light, extending 57:12's male-female light scene with a moral, rather than sexual, division.
terra: Charitable men and charitable women give God a good loan and receive multiplication; the ṣ-d-q family, giving, ḥusnā-like goodness, and both sexes share one moral measure.
terra: A wife declared to be like one's mother does not become a mother; mothers are only those who gave birth, sharply distinguishing spousehood and sexual union from maternity.
terra: The emigrant women's former bridal payments are reimbursed and new marriages require new payments, treating the marriage gift as a protected obligation across separation.

luna: The ayah measures a pregnant woman's waiting period by delivery (أَن يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ), then promises ease for whoever is mindful of God (يُسْرًا). It directly joins childbirth to ease and taqwa, as the section's 92:5–10 contrast does. | terra: Pregnant women's term ends when they lay down their burden, and the ayah then promises yusr to whoever has taqwā, directly joining delivery, fear of God, and ease as the section does.
terra: Husbands must house pregnant divorcees, spend on them until delivery, and pay for nursing, translating the section's gift and birth images into material duty.
terra: After commanding expenditure in the pregnancy context of 65:6, the ayah promises that God will make ease after hardship, joining giving, ʿusr, and yusr.
terra: The wives of Noah and Lot are not saved by marriage to righteous men, showing that spousal union does not determine a woman's moral end.
terra: Pharaoh's believing wife asks God for a house in the Garden, showing conversely that marriage to a corrupt man does not determine a woman's moral end.
terra: Mary's guarded chastity, divine breath, and faithful response repeat the birth without male approach as a boundary case to the section's ordinary reproductive scene.
terra: The exalted majesty of the Lord has neither consort nor child, distinguishing the Most High from the paired and begetting creatures He makes.

luna: This ayah begins the sequence with an emitted drop (نُطْفَةً مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ). The following verses form it and then name the two sexes, giving another direct conception-to-sex sequence. | terra: The human begins as an emitted drop, opening a compact creation sequence that reaches the male-female pair in 75:39.

luna: The section's B003 dictionary form مخلقة concerns formation of the womb's mudghah; this ayah says the drop becomes a clot and is then created and proportioned (فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ). It bridges 75:37's drop and 75:39's male/female pair. | terra: The drop becomes a clot and God creates and proportions it, linking embryonic formation to the section's خَلَقَ before 75:39 names the two sexes.

luna: This ayah says God made from it the two sexes, male and female (الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنثَىٰ), directly echoing the section's sex pair after 75:37–38's conception sequence. | terra: God makes from the embryo ٱلزَّوْجَيْنِ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰ, directly tying sexual difference to one created origin rather than to opposed value.
terra: God creates the human from a mixed drop for a test and equips him with hearing and sight, joining reproductive formation to moral purpose.
terra: After creating and equipping the human, God guides the way and leaves gratitude or ingratitude as the response, echoing 7:189-190's promised thanks and betrayal.
terra: Creation from a lowly fluid begins a four-ayah womb-and-measure sequence that answers the section's question of how male and female life begins.
terra: The fluid is placed in a secure lodging, supplying the protected and hidden womb-space developed by the section.
terra: The womb lodging holds the fluid until a known term, adding temporal measure to the hidden formation.
terra: The closing claim that God determined the process well makes divine measuring the governing action of 77:20-22.

luna: This ayah says God created humans in pairs (أَزْوَاجًا), directly paralleling the section's pairing of night/day and male/female and its claim that God creates both sexes. | terra: 'We created you in pairs' gives the human-pair premise immediately before the passage turns to sleep, night, and day.
terra: Sleep is made repose between creation in pairs and night as garment, adding bodily rest to the passage's pair-cover-day sequence.

luna: The section names the night as what covers; 78:10 says God made night a covering (لِبَاسًا). This is a direct parallel to the opening night image and to the clothing language of 2:187. | terra: Night is made a garment, echoing both the covering oath and the spouses-as-garments scene of 2:187 after 78:8's creation in pairs.

luna: This ayah makes day a time of livelihood, completing 78:10's night covering. Its day/night division parallels the section's night that veils and day that opens. | terra: Day is made for livelihood after night as garment, completing the pair's alternation from covering to an opened field of action.
terra: Pharaoh's claim to be the lord most high is the false human seizure of the height-title that the section reserves for God.

luna: The section names the root خ ل ق for the formed womb-lump; this ayah says God created the human from a drop and proportioned him (خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ). It connects embryonic origin with measured creation. | terra: Creation from a drop followed by divine measuring, خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ, supplies the section's womb-stage and its claim that created life is fitted and apportioned.

luna: The section cites 92:7's ease and links birth's exit to life's path; this ayah says God made the path easy (السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ). The shared ease root gives the section's birth/path connection a Quranic counterpart. | terra: After creation and measuring in 80:19, ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ makes the way easy, allowing the section to hear both emergence from the womb and the path of life.

luna: This ayah names the buried-alive girl (الْمَوْءُودَةُ), the stark endpoint of the section's account of devaluing daughters at birth. The following ayah asks for what sin she was killed. | terra: The buried girl is herself brought forward and questioned, reversing the father's power to hide or erase the unwanted female child.

luna: This ayah asks the buried girl for what sin she was killed (بِأَيِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ), completing 81:8. It makes the section's reversal of the male-over-female birth measure a direct moral boundary. | terra: The question 'for what sin?' declares the girl's innocence and condemns the endpoint of the dark preference staged in 16:58-59.
terra: God's creating, proportioning, and balancing of the human closely joins the section's creation word to its concern with making a body fit.
terra: God composes the human in whatever form He wills, completing 82:7 with divine choice over embodied form rather than a human scale of preferred sex.
terra: The command that a human consider what he was created from opens the reproductive examination answered in 86:6-7.
terra: Creation from a gushing fluid names the generative material behind the male-female birth scene.
terra: The fluid's emergence from within the body develops the hidden bodily origin introduced in 86:5-6, though its anatomical wording is distinct from the womb passages.
terra: The command to glorify the name of the Lord al-Aʿlā takes up the section's final height-word and introduces the creation-guidance sequence of 87:2-3.
terra: God creates and proportions, joining خَلَقَ to fitness immediately before measuring and guidance.
terra: God measures and guides, فَقَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ, placing the section's creation, fitting, and hidaya in one compact sequence.

luna: The section's B003 dictionary form جلاها describes a bride being unveiled and seen; 91:3 uses جَلَّاهَا for daylight disclosing the sun. The shared root and display scene make the section's daylight-as-opening image concrete. | terra: Day is sworn by when it reveals the sun, using ج ل و for the same daylight unveiling that the section hears as bridal disclosure.

luna: The section names غ ش و for night covering and sexual covering; this ayah uses يَغْشَاهَا for night covering the sun, paired with 91:3's daylight disclosure. It supplies the other half of the section's night/day opposition. | terra: Night is sworn by when it covers the sun, placing the غ ش و counter-action directly beside 91:3's unveiling.
terra: The assurance that with hardship comes ease refuses the old formula's permanent assignment of ʿusr to one sex and yusr to the other.
terra: The repeated assurance makes ease accompany the same hardship, reinforcing that these conditions are divinely related rather than biologically gendered.
terra: Creation of the human from a clinging form gives another concise embryonic use of خَلَقَ relevant to the section's formed flesh-piece.
terra: 'He neither begets nor is begotten' marks the sharp theological boundary between the Creator invoked in 92:3 and the male-female generation He creates.
